newsitem.title: USA: Jury selection starts in Miami hijacking trial.
newsitem.headline: Jury selection starts in Miami hijacking trial.

text.p: Jury selection was scheduled to begin Tuesday in the trial of a Palestinian man charged with using a fake bomb and a makeshift knife to hijack an Iberia Airlines jet and divert it from Cuba to Miami.

U.S. District Judge Lenore Nesbitt was expected to begin with a pool of 50 jurors in selecting the panel for the trial of Saad'o Mohamed Ibrahim Intissar. A court official said the judge's usual practice is to select two alternates in addition to the panel of 12 jurors.

Intissar is accused of commandeering Iberia Flight 6621 on July 26 as it travelled from Madrid to Havana, carrying 231 passengers and crew. The DC-10 landed safely in Miami, where Intissar immediately surrendered.

U.S. authorities said Intissar, who has pleaded not guilty to air piracy, used a fake bomb made from an electric shaver, batteries and wire, along with a makeshift knife made of a scissor blade and a wad of tape, to take over the aircraft and force it to land in the United States.
They said Intissar was born to Palestinian parents in a south Lebanon refugee camp. A Lebanese security source has said he is not a Lebanese national.
If convicted Intissar would face a minimum mandatory sentence of 20 years in prison.
